descriptor: State-controlled P&C-led Chinese insurance group (PICC P&C/Life/Health) · reported in CNY · quoted in HKD

sections.title: Growth & Profitability
sections.subtitle: Revenue mixes insurance service revenue with volatile investment income; attributable profit is after an NCI share of ~26-30%

charts.title: Net Income: Owners vs Minority Interests
charts.annotation: The gap is NCI's ~26-30% share of PICC P&C (31.0% minority), PICC Life (20%) and PICC Health (4.55%) profit.

sections.title: Book Value & Capital Structure
sections.subtitle: Debt/cash/FCF ratios do not apply to an insurer; equity, NCI and float scale are the drivers that matter

charts.title: Total Equity vs Owners' Shareholders' Equity
charts.annotation: Owners' equity is the DCF's book-value cross-check (RMB7.71/share at H1 2026, vs the H-share price at 0.56x and A-share at 0.98x).

charts.title: Securities Sold Under Repurchase Agreements
charts.annotation: Repo funds the investment portfolio, not operations; the DCF nets it inside the investment-yield definition rather than treating it as financial leverage.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For PICC Group: total liabilities run ~79% of total assets, which is structurally high but normal for an insurer carrying policyholder reserves and investment-funding repo -- it is not operating leverage the way it would be for an industrial company.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity outside of normal reserve build
  • Solvency ratios (core 197.7%, comprehensive 246.6% at H1 2026) in the Analysis JSON, which this balance sheet view does not show directly

epsDps.title: EPS and diluted EPS
epsDps.content:
EPS is attributable net income per share; diluted EPS adjusts for any dilutive instruments.

For PICC Group: there is no share-based payment scheme at Group level and no convertibles, so diluted EPS tracks basic EPS almost exactly (FY2025 basic 1.04 vs diluted 1.00, reflecting a subsidiary-level adjustment, not Group dilution). The share count has been flat at 44,224m since the 2018 A-share IPO.

What to watch:

  • FY2025/H1 2026 EPS is peak-cycle, driven by an A-share rally in the investment book, not a step-change in underwriting
  • Payout ratio (dividend per share / EPS) rising from 21% toward management's market-value-management push

equitySplit.title: Total equity vs owners' equity
equitySplit.content:
Total equity includes non-controlling interests (NCI); shareholders' equity is the portion attributable to Group owners (and therefore to H-shareholders).

For PICC Group: NCI is RMB121,696m, or 26.3% of total equity, at H1 2026 -- the minority stakes in PICC P&C (31.0%), PICC Life (20%) and PICC Health (4.55%). Only the owners' line is relevant to per-share book value.

What to watch:

  • NCI growing faster than owners' equity (dilution of the Group's claim on its own subsidiaries)
  • Owners' equity per share vs the H-share price (currently ~0.56x book) and the A-share price (~0.98x)

margins.title: Net margin
margins.content:
Net margin is attributable net income over total revenue (insurance revenue plus investment income and other).

For PICC Group: gross/operating margin concepts do not exist for an insurer -- the line shown is net margin only. It swings with the investment cycle as much as underwriting: Q1 2026 attributable profit fell 31.4% on markets alone, then H1 2026 overall was +40.4% as markets recovered.

What to watch:

  • Margin swings driven by investment gains/losses rather than the P&C combined ratio (97.5% FY2025, 94.0% H1 2026)
  • Interim vs full-year margin divergence from a weak or strong second half

nciSplit.title: Owners vs minority interests
nciSplit.content:
Attributable to owners is net income after non-controlling interests; incl. minority interests is the Group's full consolidated profit before that split.

For PICC Group: PICC P&C is 68.98% owned, PICC Life 80% and PICC Health 95.45%, so roughly 26-28% of consolidated profit belongs to minorities every year (attributable share has run 72-74% of consolidated profit FY2023-H1 2026). The DCF charges this NCI share once, inside the margin, rather than as a separate deduction.

What to watch:

  • The attributable share drifting materially from ~73-74% (a change in subsidiary ownership or profit mix)
  • Whether growth in consolidated profit is translating into attributable profit at the same rate

premiums.title: Gross premiums written
premiums.content:
Gross premiums written (original premiums income) is the cash premium volume written across P&C, life and health before any IFRS 17 service-margin recognition adjustment -- the industry's standard top-line KPI.

For PICC Group: this is a cleaner growth signal than the CSV's "Revenue" line, which is insurance revenue (service-margin recognition) plus a large and volatile investment-income component. Original premiums grew 6.5% in FY2025 against industry growth of 7.4%; PICC Life's regular premiums were the fastest-growing component (+32.4%).

What to watch:

  • Premium growth vs industry growth (market share gain or loss)
  • Mix shift toward life/health regular premiums, which carry better embedded value than single-premium or motor business

repo.title: Securities sold under repurchase agreements
repo.content:
Repo liabilities are securities sold under repurchase agreements -- short-term funding secured against the investment portfolio.

For PICC Group: this is investment-operations funding, not corporate debt. The DCF nets it inside the investment-yield definition and does not add it to net debt (net debt is held at zero for insurers in this framework). It moved from RMB180,763m (FY2025) to RMB141,482m (H1 2026).

What to watch:

  • Repo scale relative to the RMB2.0tn investment book (a funding-leverage signal, not solvency)
  • Large swings that coincide with investment-income swings, since repo often funds the equity allocation that drives the volatility seen in net margin

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue here is insurance revenue (IFRS 17 service-margin recognition) plus total investment income and other income -- not gross premiums collected.

For PICC Group: the FY2023 IFRS 17 transition broke comparability with earlier years (FY2022 615,732 vs FY2023 553,467 on the new basis), and the H1 2026 step-up (+9.6%) was driven mainly by investment income (+62.7%) during an A-share rally, not premium growth (insurance revenue was only +2.4%). See the Gross Premiums Written chart for the cleaner operating KPI.

What to watch:

  • How much of a revenue move is investment income vs insurance revenue
  • Growth relative to gross premiums written, which moves on a different basis

dcf.growth_hint: Base-case revenue growth, fading from 4.5% toward 3%
